story.description: Explore Genesis 6–9, prepare the ark, and reflect on GOD's covenant.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Genesis describes a world filled with violence. GOD told Noah about the coming flood and instructed him to prepare an ark. Read the account in your Bible as you explore this adventure.

dialogue.speaker: God
dialogue.text: Make yourself an ark of gopher wood. Make rooms in the ark, and cover it inside and out with pitch.

objective.hint: Use the word in the passage.
objective.instruction: Read Genesis 6:14. What wood does the quoted verse name?
objective.scripture: Make yourself an ark of gopher wood. Make rooms in the ark, and cover it inside and out with pitch.
objective.title: Read the ark instructions

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The quoted text says gopher wood. Its precise identity is uncertain. The wood pictures in this activity are imagined illustrations, not an identification of the Biblical tree.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The ark instructions give a length of 300 cubits, a breadth of 50 cubits and a height of 30 cubits. A cubit is a historical unit of length; this activity compares the stated dimensions.

objective.hint: Read Genesis 6:14–16 in your Bible, then answer the question.
objective.instruction: Choose the covering specified for the ark.
objective.scripture: Make yourself an ark of gopher wood. Make rooms in the ark, and cover it inside and out with pitch.
objective.title: Ark blueprint: covering

objective.hint: Read Genesis 6:14–16 in your Bible, then answer the question.
objective.instruction: Choose the door location stated in the passage. The text does not specify left or right.
objective.title: Ark blueprint: door

objective.hint: Read Genesis 6:14–16 in your Bible, then answer the question.
objective.instruction: Choose the number of decks described in Genesis 6:16.
objective.title: Ark blueprint: decks

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The passage describes rooms, a roof, a side door and three decks. Assemble the illustrated pieces in the construction puzzle. These shapes are a game representation, not a historical blueprint.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Genesis records Noah carrying out GOD's instructions. It also describes gathering food for the people and animals. The pictured foods are game examples, not a Biblical food list.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Genesis 7 distinguishes seven pairs of clean animals and birds from a pair of animals that are not clean. The matching game shows example pairs and does not represent the complete animal count or identify every Biblical kind.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Noah entered with his wife, his three sons and their wives. The clothing and faces in this game are imagined. Read Genesis 7 to see who entered and what happened next.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The account describes the LORD shutting Noah in, forty days and nights of rain, and waters prevailing for 150 days. Game stages condense the account; they are not a day-by-day timeline.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Genesis says GOD remembered Noah and the animals. A wind blew and the waters subsided. Noah sent a raven before the dove; the next activity focuses on the dove's three journeys.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: After leaving the ark, Noah built an altar. Read Genesis 8:18–22 and consider how Noah responded. The story continues with GOD's covenant.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: GOD's covenant concerns living creatures and the promise about a flood destroying all flesh. The bow in the clouds is its sign. This color-building activity illustrates a rainbow; Scripture does not give a required color order.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Return to Genesis 6–9 in your Bible. Consider GOD's judgment, Noah's response, and the covenant. Completing activities is an opportunity to reflect and keep reading.

story.title: Noah's Ark
